title: Violence named plainly, never shown
statement: Name a text's violent events plainly and seriously, without sensation, but never show the act or picture death or graphic harm.
example: In one Grade 9 unit film, each of the 13 generated paintings was checked by eye for a depicted death.
detail: The info sheet for a Grade 9 unit film, dated 2 October 2026, asks for a serious, not sensational tone at the tragedy's turning point: name the death plainly and move on, and don't show the killing, since the line on screen is enough (`g9/library/text/Lbde498.txt`, lines 69 and 80). The film's illustration log records that every generated painting was reviewed by eye on 2026-10-06 against a rule of no depicted death, and the shot that names who will die shows three candles out, one guttering, and a handkerchief (`g9/library/text/Lc52cc8.txt`, lines 5 and 15).
against: The by-eye check is the only one recorded: the same log lists the paintings as not yet reviewed beyond it (`g9/library/text/Lc52cc8.txt`, line 5). The project handover is only permissive, saying that no graphic depiction of the death is needed (line 55 of the handover text in the evidence).
